results.title: VALCO returns to profitability with $1.4m positive EBITDA in first nine months of 2026
results.content: The Volta Aluminium Company Limited (VALCO) has recorded a positive EBITDA of $1.4 million for the first nine months of 2026, reversing a $13.08 million negative EBITDA recorded during the same period last year. The financial recovery, covering the period ending September 30, 2026, was supported by increased revenue, value-added aluminium manufacturing and changes to the company's production shift system. VALCO's revenue rose by 13 per cent to $103.85 million, compared with $91.78 million recorded between January and September 2025. The company's Chief Executive Officer, Dr Robert Makila Sambian, announced the figures on November 3, 2026, during the Progress Series organised by the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources to highlight developments in Ghana's industrial sector.

results.title: Ten new scholars join Drive to Inspire – Africa, continuing scholars receive laptops
results.content: Ten new tertiary students have joined the Drive to Inspire – Africa LBG (DTI-A) scholarship programme, while some continuing scholars have received laptops to support their academic work. The awards were presented at a scholarship ceremony in Accra on October 30, 2026, organised by DTI-A in partnership with the Sanjeev Mansotra Foundation (SMF). The new beneficiaries were selected through a competitive process based on academic excellence and financial need. Their scholarships were funded by SMF under a partnership announced on April 21, 2026. The latest cohort marks the first time male tertiary students have been admitted to the DTI-A scholarship programme, which previously supported young women. The additional 10 beneficiaries bring the total number of scholarships awarded under the SMF-DTI-A partnership to 20.

results.title: Two bail applications for Asante Akyem North MP failed; his extradition hearing is set for Nov. 18 – Dafeamekpor
results.content: The Member of Parliament for Asante Akyem North, Ohene Kwame Frimpong, remains in custody in the Netherlands after two attempts to secure his release on bail were unsuccessful. Mr Frimpong was arrested at Amsterdam's Schiphol Airport on May 10, 2026, after arriving from Ghana, following an extradition request from the United States. The request is linked to allegations of romance scams and money laundering. Parliament subsequently confirmed his detention and engaged Ghana's diplomatic mission in The Hague. Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa also confirmed that consular assistance was being provided, including a visit to the MP while in detention.

results.title: News fatigue pushing audiences towards lighter digital content – MFWA
results.content: The Programmes Manager of the Media Foundation for West Africa (MFWA), Kwaku Krobea, says growing fatigue with hard news and political discussions is driving some audiences towards lighter and more entertaining digital content. Speaking on Joy Prime's Money Making Monday, Mr Krobea said the constant coverage of wars, deaths and political disagreements was leaving some people looking for content that offers a break from difficult news topics. He cited reports on the Russia-Ukraine war, tensions between the United States and Iran, and political debates involving the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and the National Democratic Congress (NDC) as examples of issues that could contribute to audience fatigue. "People get tired. And so then they want to consume certain forms of content," he said.

results.title: MFWA urges tech platforms to financially support media organisations
results.content: The Media Foundation for West Africa (MFWA) has called on technology companies to financially support media organisations whose content attracts audiences to their digital platforms. The Foundation's Programmes Manager, Kwaku Krobea, said digital platforms benefit from journalism produced by traditional media organisations and should contribute to their financial sustainability. Speaking on Joy Prime's Money Making Monday, Mr Krobea said technology companies must be held accountable for the value they derive from media content shared on their platforms. "Maybe the bigger conversation we should be having is, you know, the platform accountability, holding the platforms accountable to say ... people are watching you because of our content," he said.
